outcome: Since 26 January 2024 nothing has settled the Zilber-Pink conjecture for mixed Shimura varieties or semiabelian varieties over C, or any of its general cases. The in-window items are restricted cases (curves or Hodge-generic subvarieties under boundary, genericity, or field-of-definition hypotheses in Y(1)^n, Y(1)^3, and mixed Shimura varieties), a geometric variant for variations of mixed Hodge structure, a conditional reduction of the semiabelian case to the mixed case, conditional results and reformulations, and surveys. No in-window event credits an AI system with any of the mathematics.
problem_asks: Frozen statement (26 Jan 2024): for X a mixed Shimura variety or a semiabelian variety defined over C, and V a subvariety of X, V contains only finitely many atypical subvarieties. Parts: (1) the ambient class of mixed Shimura varieties over C, including pure Shimura varieties and, within them, Kuga type and abelian type; (2) the ambient class of semiabelian varieties over C, including abelian varieties and algebraic tori; (3) the quantifier, over every subvariety V of every X in (1) and (2); (4) the conclusion, that V has only finitely many atypical subvarieties. Atypical is defined relative to special subvarieties: W is atypical for V if it is a component of V intersected with a special subvariety S of codimension at least dim V - dim W + 1 (the Wikipedia article's definition, as I read it; special points in the semiabelian case are torsion points). Wording point: the frozen bullet says 'finitely many atypical subvarieties' with no qualifier. The literature, and the Wikipedia statement as I read it (page last edited 7 Nov 2025; I did not read the Jan 2024 revision), says 'finitely many maximal atypical subvarieties'. Finiteness of all atypical subvarieties and of the maximal ones differ, and each event below is recorded against both readings where it matters.

events.what_happened: Georgios Papas, 'Zilber-Pink in Y(1)^n: Beyond multiplicative degeneration', arXiv:2402.09487. Per the arXiv comment, this content was split from arXiv:2310.04943v1 (Oct 2023), and the paper is accepted in the Israel Journal of Mathematics (no volume or date given). The HTML of v3 (read to character 100000 of about 145900) states Theorem 1.4: for an irreducible curve C in Y(1)^n defined over Q-bar and not contained in a proper special subvariety, if all but at most one coordinate of C is singular at a boundary point s0 and the possibly smooth remaining coordinate is CM, then the Zilber-Pink conjecture holds for C. Theorem 1.5 gives the n = 3 case: C in Y(1)^3 meeting the boundary at (inf, zeta1, zeta2) or (inf, inf, zeta1), with zeta singular moduli. The abstract says the Zilber-Pink cases are a corollary of Large Galois orbits statements for unlikely-intersection points.
events.revisions: v1 14 Feb 2024; v2 20 Feb 2026; v3 24 Jun 2026 (current; comment says accepted in Israel J. Math; acknowledges Bijay Bhatta and Martin Orr for pointing out inaccuracies in Theorem 4.2, Corollary 4.4 and Theorem 4.5 of an earlier version).
events.delivers: Zilber-Pink, in the paper's own formulation, for curves over Q-bar in Y(1)^n meeting the boundary as Theorem 1.4 requires, and for the n = 3 boundary cases of Theorem 1.5. Restrictions: V is a curve; the ambient is Y(1)^n, a pure Shimura variety (a product of modular curves); the curve is defined over Q-bar; the boundary condition is at a single point with at most one non-singular coordinate, which must be CM.
events.remains: Curves in Y(1)^n outside the boundary hypotheses (for example, two or more smooth coordinates at the boundary point, or a non-CM smooth coordinate); curves not defined over Q-bar; all subvarieties of dimension at least two; all other pure Shimura varieties; all mixed Shimura varieties; all semiabelian varieties. So parts (1) to (4) of problem_asks are open outside this class.

Abstract (read): a survey of history and recent developments of Existential Closedness and Zilber-Pink, focusing on modular versions and variants incorporating derivatives of modular functions; says the functional analogues are presented as theorems, and that 'the paper also contains some new results and conjectures'. events.what_happened: Yu Fu and Roy Zhao, 'Algebraic Independence of Special Points on Shimura Varieties', arXiv:2405.14084 (v1 23 May 2024; v2 16 Jun 2024). Abstract (read): for a correspondence V between a connected Shimura variety S and a commutative connected algebraic group G, the V-images of any n special points outside a proper Zariski-closed subset are algebraically independent. Application: special points whose V-images lie in a finite-rank subgroup lie in a finite union of proper special subvarieties, with the bound depending only on the rank. The abstract does not describe the result as a Zilber-Pink case.
events.revisions: v1 23 May 2024; v2 16 Jun 2024 (changed notation and corrected typos).
events.delivers: Algebraic-independence and special-point statements for connected Shimura varieties with commutative algebraic group targets. Restrictions: special points (dimension zero); the ambient is a connected pure Shimura variety. The finite-union conclusion is a Zilber-Pink-shaped statement about special points, not a finiteness statement about all atypical subvarieties of an arbitrary subvariety V.
events.remains: Positive-dimensional subvarieties V; the full statement for every V in every mixed Shimura or semiabelian X; the non-special atypical loci.
events.direction: Neighbouring result: a special-point finiteness-type statement inside a restricted setting. Its direction for the bullet's statement is not established; the abstract makes no claim about atypical subvarieties.

events.what_happened: Gregorio Baldi and David Urbanik, 'Effective atypical intersections and applications to orbit closures', arXiv:2406.16628 (v1 24 Jun 2024; v2 17 Jul 2025; v3 25 Sep 2026; comment 'To appear in JEMS'). Abstract (read; I did not read the body): proposes a unifying framework for monodromically atypical intersections beyond the usual Zilber-Pink conjecture; a new proof of finiteness of maximal atypical orbit closures in each stratum of translation surfaces (matching Eskin, Filip and Wright); an algorithm for computing those orbit closures; and 'an effective and o-minimal free proof of the geometric Zilber-Pink conjecture for variations of mixed Hodge structures'. The 2025 survey by Daw (arXiv:2506.02900) cites this work as establishing the conjecture for variations of mixed Hodge structures [its Theorem 1.9].
events.revisions: v1 24 Jun 2024; v2 17 Jul 2025; v3 25 Sep 2026; 'to appear in JEMS' per the v3 comment.
events.delivers: Per the abstract: the geometric Zilber-Pink statement for variations of mixed Hodge structures (in the geometric sense that the maximal atypical part of the Hodge locus of positive period dimension lies in finitely many families, as the BKU formulation states it); and finiteness of maximal atypical orbit closures in translation-surface strata. Restrictions: the geometric (family) formulation over a base with a variation of mixed Hodge structure; the translation-surface result is a different setting.
events.remains: The non-geometric statement for a single mixed Shimura variety or a single semiabelian variety over C, as the bullet states it; the arithmetic side for Hodge-generic subvarieties of mixed Shimura varieties (see Klingler-Tayou below); the semiabelian case.

checked_by.what_they_did: accepted the paper, per the arXiv comment 'To appear in JEMS' (v3, 25 Sep 2026); I did not check the journal page

events.doubts: The geometric statement is not the bullet's statement as worded: it is about finitely many families of special subvarieties in a base carrying a variation of mixed Hodge structure, not about finitely many atypical subvarieties of an arbitrary subvariety V of a mixed Shimura or semiabelian variety. The survey (Daw 2025) calls this the conjecture for variations of mixed Hodge structures, which is the scope issue for the judging pass. The abstract's 'effective and o-minimal free' claim is unverified by me.
events.direction: Affirmative for the geometric formulation (a finiteness conclusion over families). Does not directly establish the bullet's absolute statement.

events.what_happened: Kaiyuan Gu and Chenxin Huang, 'On Special Subvarieties of the Universal Semi-abelian Scheme and Zilber-Pink Conjectures', arXiv:2410.17755 (v1 23 Oct 2024; v2 25 Oct 2024; v3 14 Sep 2026; 61 pages; no journal reference). Abstract (read, paraphrased by the fetch): classifies the special subvarieties of the universal semiabelian scheme of arbitrary toric rank, treating it as a mixed Shimura variety; shows that the Zilber-Pink conjecture for mixed Shimura varieties implies the corresponding statement for semiabelian varieties, correcting an error in an unpublished manuscript of Pink; gives a corrected relative Manin-Mumford formulation that includes subvarieties of Ribet type. The v3 comment says Theorem 1.4 of earlier versions is not correct as stated and that the paper was substantially rewritten.
events.revisions: v1 23 Oct 2024; v2 25 Oct 2024; v3 14 Sep 2026 (Theorem 1.4 of earlier versions not correct as stated; rewritten, works in arbitrary toric rank).
events.delivers: A conditional reduction: if the Zilber-Pink conjecture holds for mixed Shimura varieties, it holds for semiabelian varieties over C. Unconditionally, a classification of special subvarieties of the universal semiabelian scheme of arbitrary toric rank. No unconditional case of either conjecture.
events.remains: The mixed Shimura case itself, in full; the semiabelian case is reduced, not proved.
events.doubts: Earlier versions had an incorrect Theorem 1.4 (v3 comment). The reduction is an implication, so it adds no case of either side. The error in Pink's unpublished 2005-era manuscript is an attribution point (see disputes).
events.direction: Conditional: implies the semiabelian case from the mixed case. Neutral on whether the conjecture holds.

events.what_happened: Bruno Klingler and Salim Tayou, 'The Zilber-Pink conjecture for varieties not defined over Q-bar', arXiv:2504.00865 (v1 1 Apr 2025, the only version; math.AG and math.NT; no journal reference found). Abstract (read): proves the Zilber-Pink conjecture for subvarieties of mixed Shimura varieties 'which are not defined over Q-bar in a strong sense'; similar results for variations of mixed Hodge structure of geometric origin that are absolute. The HTML v1 gives Theorem 1.6: for a Hodge-generic irreducible closed subvariety X of a mixed Shimura variety S, if no non-trivial image of X in a quotient Shimura variety S -> S' is defined over Q-bar, then the atypical Hodge locus of X is not Zariski dense in X (their Conjecture 1.4). Theorem 1.11: for a geometric absolute VMHS on a smooth quasi-projective complex variety, if no non-trivial quotient period map factorises over Q-bar, Zilber-Pink (their Conjecture 1.2) holds for X and V. Theorem 1.12 gives equivalence with the geometric-origin case over Q-bar.
events.delivers: Zilber-Pink in the non-density form the paper uses (the atypical locus is not Zariski dense), for Hodge-generic subvarieties of mixed Shimura varieties satisfying the no-nontrivial-image-over-Q-bar hypothesis; and the analogue for absolute geometric VMHS under the analogous hypothesis. Restrictions: the Q-bar condition as stated in Theorem 1.6; Hodge-generic; the non-density conclusion rather than an explicit finiteness of maximal atypical subvarieties (the paper's Conjecture 1.2 for VMHS is phrased as finiteness of maximal atypical special subvarieties, which the authors treat as the equivalent formulation).
events.remains: Subvarieties with a non-trivial image defined over Q-bar; non-Hodge-generic subvarieties; mixed Shimura varieties in general; semiabelian varieties beyond what the reduction of Gu-Huang gives; and the finiteness formulation as the bullet states it.

events.what_happened: Christopher Daw, 'Unlikely intersections in Shimura varieties and beyond: a survey', arXiv:2506.02900 (v1 3 Jun 2025; math.NT). Abstract (read): an introduction to unlikely intersections for (pure) Shimura varieties and a review of the current state of the art. The HTML v1 (read to character 100000 of about 138500) states the Zilber-Pink conjecture for Shimura varieties and lists the known cases: varieties not defined over Q-bar (citing a corollary and, for Hodge-generic subvarieties of A_g, a theorem); curves in Y(1)^3 (Pila); asymmetric curves (Habegger-Pila), extended by Orr; curves in A_2 meeting A_0; curves in Y(1)^n with closure through (inf, ..., inf) (Daw-Orr), extended by Papas; PEL-type cases for Hodge-generic curves in A_g. It lists as open: Zilber-Pink beyond André-Oort and André-Pink-Zannier over Q-bar 'relatively sparse'. For the mixed case it says 'Zilber-Pink in the mixed setting has a rich history', and that Baldi-Urbanik 'have recently established the conjecture for variations of mixed Hodge structures'.
events.delivers: A survey. Claims no new unconditional result in the abstract. Its status section is the best single status statement I found for the pure case and its mixed-case remarks; I could not read its final part.
events.remains: The whole statement.
events.doubts: The survey's list of known cases is for the pure setting; its mixed-case remark is general. Its phrase 'established the conjecture' for VMHS refers to the geometric formulation (see Baldi-Urbanik record).
events.direction: Status statement; no direction on the bullet.

events.what_happened: Vahagn Aslanyan, Sebastian Eterovic and Guy Fowler, 'Modular Zilber-Pink for geometrically generic varieties', arXiv:2509.03160 (v1 3 Sep 2025; v2 18 Aug 2026 with minor corrections; 19 pages; no journal reference). Abstract (read): proves the modular Zilber-Pink conjecture, in Pink's formulation in terms of unlikely intersections, for subvarieties V of Y(1)^n satisfying a geometric genericity condition: no projection of V onto any dim V + 2 coordinates is defined over the algebraic numbers. Theorem 1.1 as stated in the HTML v2 (read to character 100000 of about 100200): for an irreducible V of dimension d in Y(1)^n not in a proper special subvariety, with every coordinate projection to d + 2 coordinates not definable over Q-bar, the union of V intersected with special subvarieties of dimension at most n - (d + 1) is not Zariski-dense in V. The paper notes the condition is vacuous for d >= n - 1 (where the conclusion was already known) and reduces to V not defined over Q-bar when d = n - 2. The authors use Modular Mordell-Lang and Ax-Schanuel for the j-function as inputs.
events.revisions: v1 3 Sep 2025; v2 18 Aug 2026 (19 pages, minor corrections; corrections not described on the abstract page).
events.delivers: Modular (Y(1)^n) Zilber-Pink in the non-density form, for irreducible V with the d + 2 projection non-definability hypothesis and the not-in-proper-special-subvariety hypothesis. Restrictions: ambient Y(1)^n only; the genericity hypothesis; the non-density conclusion.
events.remains: Subvarieties V having a coordinate projection to d + 2 coordinates defined over Q-bar (including all V defined over Q-bar with d <= n - 3, per the paper's own reduction); other pure Shimura varieties; all mixed Shimura varieties; all semiabelian varieties; the finiteness formulation as worded.
events.doubts: The hypothesis is strong (projections of V must be non-definable over Q-bar), so the theorem does not reach arithmetic subvarieties of Y(1)^n. The v2 minor corrections are not described on the abstract page. No external review found in my searches; talks by Fowler (UIC, 26 Aug 2025; Fields) are not checks.
events.direction: Affirmative in its class: the unlikely locus is not Zariski-dense in V under the genericity hypothesis. Cuts with the conjecture; restricted class.

events.what_happened: Christopher Daw, Martin Orr and Georgios Papas, 'Some new cases of Zilber-Pink in Y(1)^3', arXiv:2510.09603 (v1 10 Oct 2025; v2 25 Feb 2026; 42 pages; no journal reference). From the HTML v2 (read to character 100000 of about 156200): Theorem 1.3: for an irreducible curve C in Y(1)^3 defined over Q-bar and not in a proper special subvariety, if the boundary closure of C meets a modular point (a boundary point in one of the Y(1)^2 faces satisfying a modular polynomial equation), then C has only finitely many points satisfying the modular-polynomial conditions, i.e. the Zilber-Pink conjecture holds for C. Theorem 1.6 (unconditional): for a modular point b on C there is delta > 0 such that C contains only finitely many modular points of supersingular exponent delta with respect to b. The method is André's G-functions. The search summary says the v1 abstract omitted the 'close to a fixed base point' condition; I did not open v1 directly.
events.revisions: v1 10 Oct 2025; v2 25 Feb 2026 (v2 abstract adds 'close to a fixed base point' per the search summary; not verified against v1).
events.delivers: Zilber-Pink, for curves over Q-bar in Y(1)^3 whose boundary closure meets a modular point (Theorem 1.3); and an unconditional finiteness result for modular points of bounded supersingular exponent with respect to a fixed modular base point (Theorem 1.6). Restrictions: n = 3; curves over Q-bar; boundary condition for Theorem 1.3; for Theorem 1.6 only the subset of modular points with supersingular exponent delta, not all modular points on C.
events.remains: Curves in Y(1)^3 whose closure avoids a modular boundary point; the full finiteness of modular points on C (the unconditional result covers a subset); curves not defined over Q-bar; Y(1)^n for n other than 3; higher-dimensional V; all other Shimura varieties; mixed and semiabelian varieties.
events.doubts: Theorem 1.6 gives finiteness only for a restricted set of modular points (exponent delta), so it does not show the full finiteness of atypical points on C. The v1/v2 abstract wording differs, per the search summary. I found no external review or citation engaging with it in my searches; the 2025 CIRM and IAS talks are not checks.
events.direction: Affirmative for the restricted curves (Theorem 1.3); for Theorem 1.6, a finiteness result on a subset of the unlikely points.

events.what_happened: Luca Ferrigno, 'Unlikely intersections with CM abelian varieties in a family and explicit bounds for canonical heights under endomorphisms', arXiv:2601.05919 (v1 9 Jan 2026; v2 21 Jul 2026; 51 pages; math.NT and math.AG). The key ingredient is an explicit bound on canonical heights under endomorphisms. The abstract states no conditional hypotheses.

events.what_happened: Nazim Khelifa, 'On the distribution of mixed Hodge loci', arXiv:2603.20272 (v1 15 Mar 2026; v2 17 Aug 2026; 68 pages). Abstract (read): for admissible integral graded-polarised VMHS over a smooth complex base, non-empty typical Hodge locus implies a Zariski-dense full Hodge locus; with level at least 3 and large monodromy the typical locus is empty, and the full Hodge locus is a strict closed subset for its positive-dimensional factorwise part; under the Zilber-Pink conjecture for the variation, density of the transverse locus is equivalent to that of the typical locus.
events.delivers: Unconditional results on the distribution of Hodge loci for VMHS, and a conditional equivalence under Zilber-Pink. It proves no case of the Zilber-Pink conjecture.
events.remains: The Zilber-Pink conjecture itself; the bullet's statement is not addressed.
events.direction: Neighbouring; conditional on the conjecture for its Zilber-Pink dependence. Neutral on the bullet.

events.what_happened: Gregorio Baldi and David Urbanik, 'Intersections and the Bezout Range: Abelian Varieties', arXiv:2604.02186 (v1 2 Apr 2026; no comment or journal reference). Abstract (read): for subvarieties X, Y of complementary dimension in a simple abelian variety A, the intersections X cap [n]Y are zero-dimensional for all but finitely many integers n, and form an analytically dense subset of X as n varies; if dim X + dim Y < dim A, then X cap [n]Y is empty for a density-one set of n except at torsion points. The abstract calls these variants 'in the spirit of the completed Zilber-Pink philosophy'.
events.delivers: Results on intersections of a subvariety with the multiples [n]Y in simple abelian varieties. Not a case of the Zilber-Pink conjecture as worded (no atypical-subvariety finiteness claimed).

events.what_happened: Georgios Papas, 'Supersingular reduction and strongly special intersections in powers of the modular curve', arXiv:2605.00766 (v1 1 May 2026; v2 24 Jun 2026, 'revised and submitted version; title changed'). Abstract (read): assuming a Lang-Trotter-type sparsity statement for simultaneous supersingular reduction of pairs of elliptic curves, proves two Zilber-Pink-type finiteness results for Hodge-generic curves in Y(1)^n, via height bounds from André's G-function method. events.remains: Unconditional Zilber-Pink for Y(1)^n beyond the boundary cases already known; the sparsity input; mixed and semiabelian varieties; the full statement.

events.what_happened: Four manuscripts, all stated over Q̄. (1) 'The abelian Zilber–Pink conjecture' claims that for every abelian variety A over a number field K and every irreducible subvariety X ⊆ A over Q̄, X has only finitely many maximal atypical subvarieties. Atypicality is measured in S = ⟨X⟩_sp, the smallest torsion coset containing X: an irreducible Y is atypical if it is a component of X ∩ T for a torsion coset T ⊆ S with dim Y > dim X + dim T − dim S. The text also gives an equivalent form: finitely many proper atypical Y₁,…,Y_m such that every atypical subvariety lies in one of them. The route is a non-density theorem (if X lies in no proper torsion coset, X ∩ A^[dim X+1] is not Zariski dense in X, where A^[r] is the union of torsion cosets of codimension ≥ r), proved via an auxiliary sequence theorem (§§2–8), and then a reduction to maximal-atypical finiteness using Barroero–Dill Thm 1.9 and Habegger–Pila Thm 9.8 (§9). A finite-rank translated-intersection corollary is also stated. (2) 'The E×CM component of Zilber–Pink for curves in A₂' claims that a reduced irreducible Hodge-generic curve C ⊂ A₂ over Q̄ has only finitely many points s whose abelian surface is isogenous to E₁×E₂ with at least one factor CM (isogenies need not respect the polarization; the both-CM case is included). Its new input is a Galois-orbit lower bound for 'mixed' points (one CM, one non-CM factor): orbit size ≥ c·max{N(s), |disc End(F)|}^(1/42), where N(s) is the minimal degree of a product isogeny; the constant depends on C and K and is ineffective. Finiteness then follows from Daw–Orr's implication (their Thm 1.2, as corrected) and, for the both-CM and special points, Andre–Oort for A₂ (Pila–Tsimerman). (3) 'Quaternionic division points on curves in the Siegel threefold' claims that a reduced irreducible Hodge-generic closed curve C ⊂ A₂ over Q̄ has only finitely many points whose full geometric endomorphism algebra is an indefinite quaternion division algebra over ℚ. It proves a height bound h(t) ≤ c[K(t):K]^c′ for such points (Thm thm:height), via a common-relation interpolation theorem (§2) and Frobenius cross-pairings in a rank-five quadratic variation, then a counting argument: the period image would lie in a subset of the isotropic quadric of dimension ≤ 2, whereas full monodromy makes it Zariski dense. (4) 'Elliptic squares and Zilber–Pink for curves in A₂' claims that a Hodge-generic curve C ⊂ A₂ over Q̄ has only finitely many points whose abelian surface is isogenous to E² with E non-CM. It proves a Galois-orbit bound for these points in terms of the discriminant of the full endomorphism order and applies Daw–Orr's conditional counting theorem in its E² case, the orbit bound supplying its hypothesis. It then states the full curve case: for Hodge-generic C over Q̄, only finitely many points of C lie on special subvarieties of dimension ≤ 1 (this combines (4) with the companion theorems (2) and (3)), plus a special-closure corollary for every curve over Q̄.
events.delivers: Does not settle the frozen problem, which is stated over C and covers mixed Shimura and semiabelian varieties in general. What is claimed, all over Q̄ only: (a) Abelian varieties (ambient class (2), abelian case): for every abelian variety over Q̄ and every irreducible subvariety, finitely many maximal atypical subvarieties, with atypicality relative to the smallest containing torsion coset. That is the 'maximal' reading. The literal frozen reading ('finitely many atypical subvarieties') is not what is proved: the manuscript gives finitely many maximal ones and says every atypical subvariety lies in one of them, but makes no finiteness claim for the set of all atypical subvarieties. (b) A₂ (a pure Shimura variety, ambient class (1)), curves only: for Hodge-generic curves over Q̄, finitely many points on special subvarieties of dimension ≤ 1, which is the full curve case (Thm intro:zp in (4)). For a Hodge-generic curve in A₂ the atypical subvarieties are points (a special surface meets it only in points, which are not atypical there), so the 'all' and 'maximal' readings coincide in that case. That is my reading of the definition, not a statement in the manuscripts. For non-Hodge-generic curves over Q̄, the special-closure corollary gives the analogous finiteness, with codimension taken inside the smallest special S_C containing the curve. (c) Quantifier (3): all subvarieties of abelian varieties over Q̄; only curves in A₂. (d) Atypicality convention: the manuscripts take codimension inside the smallest special subvariety containing X. The frozen list does not say which ambient S it means, so the judge should check that choice. The manuscripts do not claim to resolve the conjecture as stated.
events.remains: If the claims are correct, still open: (a) the statement over C, and any X not defined over Q̄; (b) semiabelian varieties with nontrivial torus part (algebraic tori, general semiabelian varieties); (c) mixed Shimura varieties other than A₂ (Kuga type, other pure Shimura varieties); (d) for abelian varieties, finiteness of all atypical subvarieties rather than only the maximal ones; (e) subvarieties of A₂ of dimension ≥ 2; (f) effective or uniform bounds, none of which are claimed (the orbit and finiteness constants are ineffective).
events.doubts: (a) The abelian abstract calls its Q̄-restricted maximal-atypical statement 'the abelian Zilber–Pink conjecture'. The restriction to number fields appears in the theorem statement but not in the abstract's second sentence. (b) I did not check the proof of the auxiliary sequence theorem (§§2–8) line by line; the sections I read show no hedges. (c) E×CM: the Daw–Orr input is cited to the corrected arXiv v4 (2021), not the published text, and the footnote attributes the reduction-theory correction to Orr–Schnell. (d) E×CM: some steps are argued by citation rather than computed. The chart computation in Lemma boundary-comparison ends by invoking 'the fixed rational factor' and 'the fixed level datum'. Lemma family-height says an omitted finite set 'can be included by enlarging the constant'. (e) E×CM: the effective remark rests on a zero-free half-plane Re s > 7/8 for Dirichlet L-functions, cited to another OpenAI preprint. That is a very strong input, but the main theorems do not use it. (f) Quaternionic: the counting step (Prop counting-finiteness) is compressed. It says the arc has Nash coordinates 'algebraic over its real parameter' with 'transcendence degree at most one', and the quoted Habegger–Pila corollary is not restated in the section. (g) Elliptic squares: the interpolation theorem is titled 'Conditional height bound'. Its hypothesis (iv) is discharged in §07 (Prop nid:nonidentity), so the E² result depends on §07 being correct. (h) Elliptic squares: the paper calls its use of Daw–Orr Thm 1.3 'the precise E² case of the published conditional finiteness theorem'. The hypotheses in §§6.5–6.6 of Daw–Orr are cited, not restated, so the match is not checked here.; conditional on: (1) Abelian paper: no unproven hypothesis is assumed; it relies on published results only (Barroero–Dill 2021 Thm 1.9, Habegger–Pila 2016 Thm 9.8, Ax's analytic-subgroup theorem and others) and on no other family manuscript. (2) E×CM: relies on Daw–Orr's implication (their Thm 1.2, taken from the corrected arXiv v4 rather than the published 2021 text, with the reduction-theory correction of Orr–Schnell), on Siegel's class-number bound (ineffective), and on Andre–Oort for A₂ (Pila–Tsimerman). Its effective-constant remark (rem:effective-cm) uses another OpenAI manuscript, the Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis zero-free half-plane preprint (OAI:The-Quasi-Riemann-Hypothesis-September-30-2026). That manuscript is not in this family and I did not read it; the main theorems do not use the remark. (3) Quaternionic paper: no unproven hypothesis that I could identify; relies on Habegger–Pila Cor. 7.2 (quoted with k=1), Pila–Wilkie and Pila's counting results, Andre's monodromy theorem, and its own interpolation theorem (§2; I read only the statement). (4) Elliptic-squares paper: the E² theorem rests on Daw–Orr Thm 1.3 with their Conjecture 6.2, which the paper verifies for the E² locus only; it also uses Masser–Wüstholz endomorphism estimates and Andre's normality theorem. The full curve theorem (Thm intro:zp) and its special-closure corollary depend on two other family manuscripts: 'The E×CM component of Zilber–Pink for curves in A₂' (its Thm 1.1, which is item (2) here) and 'Quaternionic division points on curves in the Siegel threefold' (its Thm 1.1, which is item (3) here).

disputes.summary: Klingler-Tayou claim their theorem applies to powers of Shimura varieties, including Y(1)^n. Aslanyan, Eterovic and Fowler state that for Y(1)^n KT's Q-bar hypothesis forces every projection of V to Y(1) to be constant, so the modular case of KT reduces to the trivial case of a point. I read AEF's remark in their HTML v2; I did not verify it against KT's own text.

The 2025 Daw survey says Baldi and Urbanik 'established the conjecture for variations of mixed Hodge structures'. Baldi-Urbanik's abstract says 'the geometric Zilber-Pink conjecture'. The geometric formulation (finitely many families of special subvarieties in a VMHS base) is not the bullet's absolute statement about atypical subvarieties of V in a mixed Shimura or semiabelian variety.

Gu and Huang state that the Zilber-Pink conjecture for mixed Shimura varieties implies the semiabelian case and correct an error in an unpublished manuscript of Pink. Their v3 comment says Theorem 1.4 of earlier versions was not correct as stated.

Bertrand and Edixhoven (2019/2020) present a counterexample to the relative Manin-Mumford conjecture for families of semiabelian varieties, and read it as evidence for Pink's absolute conjecture for mixed Shimura varieties. Gu and Huang correct the relative formulation to include subvarieties of Ribet type. This is a dispute about the relative formulation, not the bullet's absolute statement.

Papas (arXiv 2402.09487) acknowledges inaccuracies in Theorem 4.2, Corollary 4.4 and Theorem 4.5 of an earlier version, pointed out by Bijay Bhatta and Martin Orr. It is not clear from what I read whether the current Theorem 1.4 and 1.5 are affected.

summary: I ran 43 web searches and opened the arXiv abstract pages, and where the fetch returned them the HTML texts, for the primary sources below, together with the Wikipedia article. The Wikipedia lead says the conjecture is a far-reaching generalisation of Andre-Oort, Manin-Mumford and Mordell-Lang, and its statement reads 'V contains only finitely many maximal atypical subvarieties'; the frozen wording lacks 'maximal', and I record both readings. No source I read says the conjecture as stated has been proved or disproved, and the literature (Pila 2025; the Daw survey 2025; the Baldi-Urbanik and Klingler-Tayou introductions as read) describes the general case as open. In-window events are restricted cases and reformulations: Papas (Feb 2024) gives Zilber-Pink for curves in Y(1)^n under boundary conditions; Gu-Huang (Oct 2024) reduces the semiabelian case to the mixed case, conditionally; Baldi-Urbanik (Jun 2024, to appear in JEMS) proves the geometric Zilber-Pink statement for variations of mixed Hodge structure; Klingler-Tayou (Apr 2025) prove the non-density form for Hodge-generic subvarieties of mixed Shimura varieties under a Q-bar hypothesis that, per AEF's remark, is trivial in the modular case; Aslanyan-Eterovic-Fowler (Sep 2025) prove the modular non-density statement under a genericity hypothesis; Daw-Orr-Papas (Oct 2025) prove Zilber-Pink for curves in Y(1)^3 under a boundary condition and a finiteness result on a subset of modular points; Ferrigno (Jan 2026) gives a relative abelian-scheme result over a Q-bar base; Dogra-Pandit (Aug 2026) claim a new proof of finiteness of the Zilber-Pink locus for curves in abelian varieties (field of definition not stated in the abstract); Papas (May 2026) gives two results conditional on a Lang-Trotter-type input. The rest are reformulations (Pila 2025, Model Theory 2024 analogue), conditional implications (Richard-Yafaev 2024, Gu-Huang), neighbouring results (Khelifa, Fu-Zhao, Baldi-Urbanik 2026, Eterovic-Scanlon) and surveys (Aslanyan 2024, Dogra 2025, Daw 2025). Pre-window: the main restricted cases are Habegger-Pila (2014), Orr (2017), Barroero-Dill (2021), Richard-Yafaev (2021, APZ in abelian type), Pila-Shankar-Tsimerman (2021, Andre-Oort in full generality, pure), Baldi-Klingler-Ullmo (2021, geometric VHS), Daw-Orr (2022), Gao-Habegger (2023, relative), and the Bertrand-Edixhoven relative counterexample (2019). Close calls for the judging pass: (a) Klingler-Tayou's conclusion is non-density, the bullet asks for finiteness of maximal atypical subvarieties, and KT's Q-bar hypothesis excludes most subvarieties of Y(1)^n; (b) Baldi-Urbanik's geometric statement is for VMHS bases and its scope relative to the bullet is contested in the literature (the survey's 'established the conjecture'); (c) Dogra-Pandit's abstract does not give the field of definition or the scope of 'new proof of finiteness', so I cannot say whether it is a new case; (d) the frozen wording's 'atypical' without 'maximal' changes what finiteness means. AI: no event credits an AI system with any of the mathematics. I read the abstracts and, for the HTML texts I opened, the statements and the portion read up to character 100000; none of these shows an AI disclosure. The one AI-disclosed preprint in this neighbourhood is Baker's 'Elliptic matroids and modular curves' (arXiv:2608.05299, 5 Aug 2026), which the fetched abstract places in matroid realisation spaces of X_1(n), not in Zilber-Pink; its AI statement (ChatGPT/GPT-5.5 Pro, GPT-5.6 Pro, and a 'Claude Fable 5' proofreading role, per search excerpts) I could not read in the PDF, and I do not record it as an event because it is not about this problem. No search found an AI-produced or AI-assisted Zilber-Pink result, and the AI-lab announcements I found (the May 2026 Erdos unit-distance result, AlphaEvolve, FrontierMath Open Problems) do not concern this statement.
competing_reading: Read event by event, the in-window record contains a real advance on this bullet's class: Klingler-Tayou (2025) prove a Zilber-Pink statement for a whole family of Hodge-generic subvarieties of mixed Shimura varieties, and Baldi-Urbanik (2024, to appear in JEMS) prove the geometric statement for all variations of mixed Hodge structure. A reader counting by 'a case of the conjecture' would count these as progress on the mixed-Shimura side. The opposing reading is that neither touches the bullet as worded: KT's conclusion is non-density under a hypothesis that is trivial for the modular case; Baldi-Urbanik's is a geometric finiteness over families; both leave every subvariety with a Q-bar-rational projection, and the semiabelian side is only reduced to the mixed side (Gu-Huang), not proved. On that reading, no event in the window settles any part of the statement, and the in-window restricted cases all sit inside the pure modular or CM-type classes.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The precise statement of Klingler-Tayou's Theorem 1.6 and the meaning of 'not defined over Q-bar in a strong sense', checked against AEF's remark that the modular specialisation is trivial. (2) The JEMS version of Baldi-Urbanik and whether its geometric theorem yields finiteness of maximal atypical subvarieties of an arbitrary subvariety V of a mixed Shimura or semiabelian variety, or only the family-level statement. (3) The full text of Dogra-Pandit: the field of definition, the 'suitably large p' and 'further assumptions', and whether the finiteness claim is new relative to Habegger-Pila. event.what_happened: Georgios Papas, 'Zilber-Pink in Y(1)^n: Beyond multiplicative degeneration', arXiv:2402.09487. Per the arXiv comment, this content was split from arXiv:2310.04943v1 (Oct 2023), and the paper is accepted in the Israel Journal of Mathematics (no volume or date given). The HTML of v3 (read to character 100000 of about 145900) states Theorem 1.4: for an irreducible curve C in Y(1)^n defined over Q-bar and not contained in a proper special subvariety, if all but at most one coordinate of C is singular at a boundary point s0 and the possibly smooth remaining coordinate is CM, then the Zilber-Pink conjecture holds for C. Theorem 1.5 gives the n = 3 case: C in Y(1)^3 meeting the boundary at (inf, zeta1, zeta2) or (inf, inf, zeta1), with zeta singular moduli. The abstract says the Zilber-Pink cases are a corollary of Large Galois orbits statements for unlikely-intersection points.
event.revisions: v1 14 Feb 2024; v2 20 Feb 2026; v3 24 Jun 2026 (current; comment says accepted in Israel J. Math; acknowledges Bijay Bhatta and Martin Orr for pointing out inaccuracies in Theorem 4.2, Corollary 4.4 and Theorem 4.5 of an earlier version).
event.delivers: Zilber-Pink, in the paper's own formulation, for curves over Q-bar in Y(1)^n meeting the boundary as Theorem 1.4 requires, and for the n = 3 boundary cases of Theorem 1.5. Restrictions: V is a curve; the ambient is Y(1)^n, a pure Shimura variety (a product of modular curves); the curve is defined over Q-bar; the boundary condition is at a single point with at most one non-singular coordinate, which must be CM.
event.remains: Curves in Y(1)^n outside the boundary hypotheses (for example, two or more smooth coordinates at the boundary point, or a non-CM smooth coordinate); curves not defined over Q-bar; all subvarieties of dimension at least two; all other pure Shimura varieties; all mixed Shimura varieties; all semiabelian varieties. So parts (1) to (4) of problem_asks are open outside this class.

judgement.why: The statement covers every subvariety of every mixed Shimura or semiabelian variety over C, so no event is whole. Restricted unconditional cases of the absolute statement score case: Papas 2024 (Israel J. Math acceptance, so digested), Klingler-Tayou, Aslanyan-Eterovic-Fowler, Daw-Orr-Papas and the OpenAI family. For Klingler-Tayou and AEF the conclusion is non-density of the atypical locus. That is the standard equivalent form of finiteness of maximal atypical subvarieties, and it is restricted by hypothesis, so case and not variant. Geometric (family-level) VMHS/VHS results, relative family results (Ferrigno, Gao-Habegger, Bertrand-Edixhoven), the Fu-Zhao special-point statement and the z^i analogue answer changed questions: variant. Conditional reductions, reformulations and surveys score none. Dogra-Pandit is also none, because its abstract calls it a new proof of a finiteness already known for curves in abelian varieties. The OpenAI repository says its results came from an internal model, so that event is generated. I marked it doubtful but kept it: it is very fresh, it claims a landmark, and its key steps were not checked.
judgement.doubts: There are two close calls. (1) Baldi-Urbanik 2024: I read the geometric Zilber-Pink statement for VMHS as a variant, not a case of the absolute statement. Daw's survey describes it as establishing the conjecture for VMHS. (2) Under the literal frozen wording, 'finitely many atypical subvarieties' without 'maximal', results proving finiteness of maximal atypical subvarieties are not literally the statement. I judged them on the standard maximal reading. If the abstract hides a new field-of-definition case, Dogra-Pandit's scope could be case. The Pila 2024 Model Theory paper is year-only, so I could not place its date.
